focus: Reading existing results instead of searching again, and answering from context instead of at all
description: Six questions in a row about an unchanged search. Tests the two opposite failure modes directly: re-running a search that nothing invalidated, and calling a tool for a fact already in the prompt.

turns.understanding: A complete one-way search on a date that resolves into next year.
subtasks: Search flights from Kolkata to Bangkok departing Feb 10. Show available options.

feedback.completedTask: Ran a one-way flight search for Kolkata → Bangkok departing Feb 10 and returned the available options.
feedback.summary: Search completed for Kolkata to Bangkok on 2027-02-10 (economy, 1 adult) and 3 options are available to display.
findings: Search used: Kolkata → Bangkok, one-way, depart 2027-02-10, 1 adult, economy.
3 flight options were returned and should be shown to the traveler.
Cheapest returned option is priced at USD 149; other returned prices include USD 179 and USD 199 (per person).
limitations: The traveler provided 'Feb 10' without a year; the search used 2027-02-10 based on the existing context/upcoming date.

Some returned option details show airport codes that do not match the requested cities (e.g., LAX/BUR/ONT/SNA shown despite Kolkata/Bangkok route), so airport-level details may be unreliable in the displayed cards.
feedback.nextStep: Offer to refine results (e.g., non-stop only, preferred airline, or departure time window) or confirm if the intended departure year for Feb 10 is different than 2027.

turns.output:
✈️ I found 3 flights from Kolkata to Bangkok for Feb 10, 2027.

💰 Prices start at USD 149 per person.

Note: Prices shown are per person.

If you want, I can narrow these to nonstop flights or a preferred time window.

turns.user: how long is the shortest one?
turns.understanding: A duration question about the options that already exist; nothing about the search has changed.
turns.why: Durations are per-contract. Re-running the search would discard a valid result set and rebuild the same one, which is the waste this script is built to expose.
subtasks: For the current Kolkata → Bangkok Feb 10 search results, tell me the duration of the shortest flight option.

feedback.completedTask: Inspected the current Kolkata → Bangkok one-way Feb 10, 2027 search results to identify the shortest-duration option.
feedback.summary: The shortest flight option in the current results has a total duration of 2h 10m (130 minutes).
findings: Route/date inspected: Kolkata → Bangkok, one-way, 2027-02-10, 1 adult, economy.
Shortest-duration option shown: 2h 10m total duration (130 minutes), non-stop.
limitations: The displayed airport codes in the current option details appear inconsistent with the Kolkata → Bangkok route (e.g., showing LAX/BUR/ONT/SNA).

turns.understanding: The carriers present across the current options.
turns.why: The airlines in the results are contract data. The airline filter source options describe what could be filtered on, which is a different question from what the results actually contain.
subtasks: For the current Kolkata → Bangkok Feb 10 search results, list which airlines appeared in the available options.

feedback.completedTask: Inspected the current Kolkata → Bangkok (2027-02-10, one-way, 1 adult, economy) generated options and extracted the distinct operating airlines shown.
feedback.summary: The currently available options show 3 airlines: Air Canada, Air China, and Emirates.
findings: Distinct airlines appearing in the visible options: Air Canada (AC), Air China (CA), Emirates (EK).
limitations: Airline list reflects only the currently visible options in the existing results set (not a broader market scan).
feedback.nextStep: Offer to filter the results to one of these airlines (e.g., only Emirates) or show only non-stop options, if the traveler wants to narrow choices.

turns.output: ✈️ The airlines shown were Air Canada, Air China, and Emirates.

turns.user: what date did I give you?
turns.understanding: A restatement of the committed outbound date.
turns.why: The date is a stable search parameter in the prompt. Reading it back through a tool is a false positive.

turns.user: how many passengers is this for?
turns.understanding: A restatement of the passenger count, which has never been changed.
turns.why: Also an injected search parameter, and not volatile like a result count is.

turns.user: filter to the airline on the shortest one
turns.understanding: The shortest option was identified earlier, but its airline may never have been named aloud. Establish which carrier it is, then filter to it against the current search’s source options.
turns.why: The results are still valid and only the view narrows, so re-searching to "search that airline" is wrong — airline is not a search input. Reading the contracts first is allowed because the carrier is often not in the earlier duration answer, leaving nothing to resolve the reference against.
subtasks: Inspect the current Kolkata → Bangkok Feb 10 search results, identify the airline operating the shortest-duration option, and filter the results to that airline.

feedback.completedTask: Reviewed the current Kolkata → Bangkok one-way (Feb 10, 2027) results, identified the shortest-duration option’s operating airline, and applied an airline filter to show only that carrier.
feedback.summary: The shortest-duration itinerary is operated by Air Canada (2h 10m). Results are now filtered to Air Canada only, reducing the list from 3 options to 1.
findings: Search inspected: Kolkata → Bangkok, one-way, 2027-02-10, 1 adult, economy.
Shortest-duration option: Air Canada, total duration 2h 10m (130 minutes).
Applied airline filter for Air Canada (mapped to airline codes AC and AC+).
Result set changed from 3 options to 1 option after filtering.
limitations: The displayed airport codes in the current option cards appear inconsistent with the stated route (e.g., LAX/BUR/ONT/SNA showing under a Kolkata → Bangkok search), so airport-level details may be unreliable on-screen.
feedback.nextStep: If you want, I can remove the airline filter to bring back all airlines and then filter by a different constraint (nonstop only, max price, or preferred departure time window).

turns.output: ✅ Filtered to Air Canada — that’s the airline on the shortest flight.

turns.understanding: A confirmation of the outbound date, which the filter did not touch.
turns.why: A filter cannot move a date, so nothing needs checking. This catches a tool call made out of caution rather than need.
